To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) psychological disturbances in the ICU are not due to the presence of a single organ system dysfunction, but are a result of multiple system failures; 2) the treatment of such psychological disturbances is a process of restoring the integrity of the patient's total system.

(1) the ICU is not a place where the patient is in an altered state of consciousness, but rather a place where consciousness is altered; and (2) the altered state of consciousness is a function of the environment and the pathophysics of the patient.

(1) psychological factors are important in the ICU; (2) psychological factors can be measured; (3) psychological factors can predict outcome in the ICU; and (4) psychological factors can influence the course of disease in the ICU.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the assessment and treatment of the patient in a state of multisystem failure.
the study of the relationship of psychological disturbances to physiological dysfunction and with the development of a unified treatment approach.
the study of behavioral and psychological disturbances of the critically ill patient and the development of a unified approach to therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the psychological disturbances in the ICU are a reflection of the severity of the illness and the degree of disability.
a unified approach to behavioral problems in the ICU is the best approach.
the ICU is an ideal environment for the development of a new model of the mind-body relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
psychological problems are best managed in a multidisciplinary approach.
a patient's ability to function in the ICU is determined by the interrelationships of the various components of the total system.
a patient's psychological state can be improved by improving other systems in the patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
psychological factors in the intensive care unit can be treated successfully.
psychological problems are not a separate category, but are an integral part of the patient's illness.
a unified approach to the patient's total system can be more efficient in the treatment of the patient than a single system approach.
